findings.claim: c3 consult --rev with the http engine warns but still sends a pack of the live working tree to a remote model, while the operator asked for a frozen revision.

evidence.observation: plan_isolation returns Ok(None) for engine http, so no worktree is made; the caller only pushes a WARNING string and continues the run.
Patch wires rev/diff through for every engine but the --rev isolation is skipped for http with a printed WARNING, not a refusal; the http pack path still reads the live tree.

findings.remedy: Refuse --rev with the http engine before anything starts, or build the pack from the resolved sha worktree instead of warning and sending live content.
findings.trigger: c3 consult --rev <old> --engine http (or panel/MCP with rev) in a tree whose live files differ from <old>, including uncommitted secrets.
findings.verification: Run --rev with the http engine and capture which tree the pack is built from; confirm no network send occurs after the warning.

findings.claim: --diff with one revision (diff against the working tree) includes every untracked non-ignored file, so an unrelated secret file in the checkout is written into the handoff patch and handed to the reviewer, including a remote model.

evidence.observation: WorkingTree path lists untracked files with ls-files --others --exclude-standard, marks them intent-to-add in a temp index copy, then diffs the rev; ignored files are excluded but ordinary untracked files are all included.
No prompt, warning, or path filter narrows the untracked set to review-relevant files before the patch is named in the prompt and sent.

findings.remedy: Limit WorkingTree --diff to tracked changes by default and require an explicit flag to include untracked files, with a warning naming the included untracked paths.
findings.trigger: c3 consult --diff HEAD in a checkout containing an untracked non-ignored secret file, reviewed by any engine that sends the patch off machine.
findings.verification: Place an untracked secret-named file in a scratch repo, run --diff HEAD, and inspect whether the patch bytes contain it.

findings.claim: Two concurrent runs sharing one brief stem but different --diff ranges write the same patch path, so the loser's ledger sha256/files/bytes can describe bytes the winner wrote.

evidence.observation: plan_diff derives the patch name only from the brief stem (or nn/prefix), never from the range; write_patch treats identical bytes as fine but different bytes from a sibling race as fine too after re-checking same().
Ledger diff record is filled from the in-memory plan after the write, so a same-path overwrite by a sibling between write and commit binds the entry to the wrong file.

findings.remedy: Include a short hash of the normalized range in the patch filename, or fail the write when the path already holds different bytes instead of accepting the race.
findings.trigger: Two c3 consult --diff runs (or two panel members with different diffs) on the same task/brief with different ranges at the same time.
findings.verification: Run two --diff specs with the same brief concurrently and compare each ledger diff.sha256 with the sha256 of the file at its patch path.

findings.claim: The throwaway worktree owner record is still best-effort, so a live --rev/kimi/claude worktree whose owner write failed can be reaped by doctor --fix while the reviewer is running.

evidence.observation: ThrowawayWorktree::create calls record_throwaway_owner and discards its result; an unrecorded live worktree is indistinguishable from a stale one to the 6-hour staleness rule.

findings.remedy: Check the owner-write result and fail the run as a capability failure when it cannot be recorded, or make staleness require positive proof of death rather than a missing owner file.
findings.trigger: Owner write fails (read-only admin dir, concurrent cleanup) and doctor --fix runs more than 6 hours after the worktree directory mtime while the reviewer process is alive.
findings.verification: Make record_throwaway_owner fail in a fixture, start a kimi/--rev run, then run doctor --fix and check the live worktree survives.

findings.claim: consult --rev/--diff performs repository writes (patch file, staged worktree metadata, worktree registration) even when C3_CHILD=1, and MCP rev/diff values reach git argument construction through only the CLI syntax check.

evidence.observation: Search shows no C3_CHILD guard on the consult patch/worktree setup path; prepare_review_inputs writes the patch into the live handoffs before the first turn unconditionally.
MCP maps rev/diff straight to --rev/--diff CLI flags; the only gate before git is rev_token_ok/parse_diff_spec syntax, with semantic resolve done later in orchestration.

findings.remedy: Honor C3_CHILD=1 on the patch write (refuse or redirect outside the repo) and document the MCP rev/diff contract; add MCP-side length/charset validation mirroring the CLI.
findings.trigger: A C3-started child (C3_CHILD=1) runs c3 consult --diff, or an MCP caller supplies rev/diff with unusual but syntax-valid tokens.
findings.verification: With C3_CHILD=1 run consult --diff in a scratch repo and check whether a patch file is created; pass boundary rev/diff strings via MCP and confirm they are refused before git.

findings.claim: Under --rev the review reads an older commit but findings bookkeeping stays bound to live HEAD, so a verdict/findings can be recorded against code that was never reviewed.

evidence.observation: Brief states findings stay bound to the live HEAD even under --rev; the isolation plan pins sha for the worktree while the ledger entry still carries the live base commit.
No re-binding of open/prior findings to the reviewed sha is described in reviewed.rs or the orchestration hunks; the resume warning only warns on thread reuse.

findings.remedy: Bind the findings snapshot to the reviewed sha under --rev (or label the entry unbound), and warn that prior HEAD findings were not re-checked at that revision.
findings.trigger: Review an older revision with open findings recorded against current HEAD; inspect which commit the resulting findings attach to.
findings.verification: Open a finding on HEAD, run --rev on an older sha, and read the committed entry's base/findings linkage.

reply_markdown:
Q1 Same revision: panel resolves once to a full sha and members check out that sha, and single runs pin the sha before worktree add, so a moving branch does not split runs. Blob/tree shas are refused by `^{commit}` plus the 40-hex check. Weak points: prefix-equality in resume_revision_warning can equate distinct shas sharing a 12-char prefix, and findings stay bound to live HEAD while the code read is an older sha (false attribution, finding #6). Shallow clones fail as capability failures, which is safe.

Q2 Staging: copies only task handoffs (minus `.events.jsonl`), `state.md`, and a stageable brief. Source links are skipped, dest links and link-parents refuse, and `..`/absolute brief refs are not staged (unreachable ones are refused). No write through a checked-out link was found. Overwrite of a tracked path happens only inside the throwaway. Hard-link sources are copied by content, not linked.

Q3 Diff/index: range sides reject leading `-` and whitespace, and the range is passed as one argv, so option injection was not found. Temp-index path uses a uuid copy with `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, leaving the real index alone. Gaps: WorkingTree `--diff` sweeps every untracked non-ignored file into the patch (finding #2); same patch path for different ranges races the ledger (finding #3). Binary/file counting via `diff --git` lines understates binaries.

Q4 Cleanup: one worktree per run dropped after the commit covers success/failure/timeout paths, and removal stays link-safe. SIGKILL/detach-kill leaves Drop unrun for doctor, but the owner record is best-effort so a live tree can look stale (finding #4). A failed worktree create after a patch write leaves the patch behind.

Q5 Classification/races: live-tree changes are now warnings for isolated reviewers and worktree writes decide the outcome; sibling worktrees use distinct uuid dirs. Remaining risk is claude/grok/muse writes staying usable by design, and the patch-path race above. No name collision beyond the patch path was found.

Q6 Privacy/entry: http+--rev warns yet sends the live pack off machine (finding #1, blocker). Frozen-claude isolation lines now send up to 20 live uncommitted paths to the model endpoint. MCP forwards rev/diff to CLI flags with only syntax checks, and C3_CHILD=1 does not stop the patch write (finding #5). CHANGELOG overstates link safety by implying no `--force`, while the code runs `worktree remove --force` after the unlink pass.

Q7 Untested: no real-CLI run of --rev/--diff/HEAD worktree is on record; Windows junction/dir-symlink removal, doctor-after-crash discovery, detached-kill cleanup, MCP boundary strings, and C3_CHILD behavior are covered only by fakes or not at all. Prior findings were not re-run; all are reported still-open.

## Requested checks
RC1 Run `c3 consult --rev <old> --engine http` in a scratch repo and confirm which tree the pack contains. Needs workspace-write. Settles finding #1.
RC2 Run `c3 consult --diff HEAD` with an untracked non-ignored sentinel file and inspect the patch bytes. Needs workspace-write. Settles finding #2.
RC3 Run two `--diff` ranges sharing one brief concurrently and compare each ledger `diff.sha256` with the file on disk. Needs workspace-write. Settles finding #3.
RC4 Make `record_throwaway_owner` fail, start a kimi/--rev run, then run `c3 doctor --fix` while it lives. Needs workspace-write. Settles finding #4.
RC5 With `C3_CHILD=1`, run `c3 consult --diff HEAD` and check whether a patch file is created. Needs workspace-write. Settles finding #5.
